chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in giving the man two, three, or four [units]," meaning the fitrah [alms of Ramadan]."

key_terms.الرَّأْسَيْنِ: Two units (typically referring to qirat or dirhams of food/currency)
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةَ: Fitrah, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of fitrah that can be given to one person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the flexibility in Zakat al-Fitr distribution, allowing a single recipient to receive multiple units (two, three, or four) rather than being limited to one. This ruling addresses the practical concern of whether splitting the fitrah among multiple poor individuals is preferable or if concentrating it on one is valid, affirming the latter's permissibility. The mention of 'two, three, or four' reflects the common denominations of currency or food measures used in the early Shia scholarly tradition to ensure the recipient's sufficiency.
